summary: This document describes Information Elements related to the data link layer. IPFIX uses them to encode measured data link layer traffic information.

eli5.summary: Network measurement reports have named boxes to fill in. This adds more boxes for facts about the lowest layer, which is the wire-level part of the network.

questions: ipfix data link layer information elements
how to export layer 2 flow data
what is an i-tag in ethernet
subtitle: New and revised IPFIX Information Elements for measuring Ethernet and other data link layer traffic.

tldr.problem: Ethernet and VLANs moved from local networks into wide-area carrier networks and data centers, with many header formats. The IPFIX and PSAMP information models did not have enough Information Elements for the data link layer.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists existing and new Information Elements for data link frames, layer 2 counters, Provider Backbone Bridge service tags and packet section offsets. It also revises the descriptions of several existing elements.
tldr.outcome: The new elements were allocated in the IANA IPFIX registry, which is the ultimate reference. The RFC does not update RFC 5477 or RFC 7011.

today: RFC 7133 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The RFC itself says IANA's IPFIX registry is the ultimate reference for these Information Elements.

sections.title: Why Data Link Layer Measurement
sections.content:
Ethernet and VLAN technologies had been used only in Local Area Networks. They are now used in Wide Area Networks, for example Layer 2 VPN services, and carrier networks have been enhanced to Provider Bridged Networks and Provider Backbone Bridged Networks (IEEE802.1Q). Ethernet in data centers has also been enhanced for server virtualization and I/O consolidation.

These changes add flexibility but also complicate traffic measurement because of the many Ethernet header formats. IPFIX and Packet Sampling (PSAMP) can help, but the PSAMP information model (RFC 5477) and the IPFIX one did not contain enough Information Elements for the data link layer.

The RFC states that it does not update RFC 5477 or RFC 7011, because IANA's IPFIX registry is the ultimate Information Element reference, per RFC 7012.
sections.eli5: Networks used to be small and simple. Now they are big and have many kinds of labels on each message, so the people who count traffic need more names for what they see.

sections.title: Extended Ethernet Technology
sections.content:
Wide-area Ethernet. In a Provider Bridge there are two VLAN IDs: the Service VLAN Identifier (S-VID), assigned by the service provider, and the Customer VLAN Identifier (C-VID), assigned by the customer. Switching in the provider network is based only on the S-VID. A Provider Backbone Bridge adds the Backbone VLAN Identifier (B-VID) and the Backbone Service Instance Identifier (I-SID). Switching uses a 12-bit B-VID, and customer identification uses a 24-bit I-SID. This lets service providers separate network management from customer management.

Virtual Ethernet. In data centers, virtual switches make it hard to monitor traffic among virtual machines. The IEEE 802.1 group standardizes Edge Virtual Bridging with Virtual Edge Bridge (VEB) and Virtual Edge Port Aggregator (VEPA), and Bridge Port Extension. They use S-channel (with an S-TAG) and E-channel (with an E-TAG). These tag values only have local meaning and flows are reported on the corresponding virtual ports, so IPFIX does not need to monitor data based on these tags.
sections.eli5: Big networks add extra stickers to each message, like an outer envelope for the carrier and an inner one for the customer. This section explains the stickers.

sections.title: Existing and New Information Elements
sections.content:
Section 3 groups the elements in three sets. The first set supports the data link layer in general, and is not limited to Ethernet. The second supports IEEE802.1Q. The third is layer 2 octet counters and packet lengths.

Existing elements (3.1). dataLinkFrameSize (312) gains the Data Type Semantics quantity. dataLinkFrameSection (315) is extended to refer to the new sectionOffset: it carries n octets starting sectionOffset octets into the frame, and a missing offset means zero. The layer 2 counters layer2OctetDeltaCount (352), layer2OctetTotalCount (353), layer2FrameDeltaCount (430) and layer2FrameTotalCount (431) are reproduced unchanged.

New elements (3.2). dataLinkFrameType (408) is a flags value, where 0x01 is IEEE 802.3 Ethernet and 0x02 is the IEEE 802.11 MAC frame format. Because the values are bits, multiple observations can be OR'd together. sectionOffset (409) and sectionExportedOctets (410) describe a packet section; octets beyond sectionExportedOctets in a fixed-size section MUST be zero-valued padding. Elements 411 to 415 expose the I-TAG, and 417 to 429 are layer 2 versions of existing octet counters, such as dropped, ignored, not sent, minimum and maximum lengths, and sums of squares.

Each new layer 2 counter points to the existing element it mirrors, for example postL2OctetDeltaCount is the layer 2 version of postOctetDeltaCount (ElementId 23).
sections.eli5: It is like a form with named boxes. Some boxes already existed, a few got clearer instructions, and many new boxes were added for counting bytes and frames on the wire.

sections.title: Packet Sections and VLAN Tag Updates
sections.content:
The new sectionOffset and sectionExportedOctets apply to all packet section elements, so Section 4 updates their descriptions: ipHeaderPacketSection (313), ipPayloadPacketSection (314), mplsLabelStackSection (316) and mplsPayloadPacketSection (317). Without a matching sectionOffset, the octets MUST start at the beginning of the section. Without a sectionExportedOctets, the element SHOULD be variable length and MUST NOT be padded. The text also notes that full packet capture of arbitrary packet streams is explicitly out of scope.

Section 5 revises the VLAN tag elements dot1qVlanId (243), dot1qPriority (244), dot1qCustomerVlanId (245) and dot1qCustomerPriority (246) so they cover S-TAG, C-TAG and B-TAG in Provider Bridged and Provider Backbone Bridged Networks. The I-TAG has a different structure, so it gets the separate elements added in Section 3. In a multi-tagged frame, the first two describe the outer tag, except for the I-TAG.
sections.eli5: Some old boxes now say more exactly which sticker on the message they are about, and a new box says how far into the message you started copying.

sections.title: Ethernet Header Fields and Their Elements
sections.content:
Section 6 shows three frame layouts and which Information Elements represent each field. A customer-tagged frame holds C-DA (6 octets), C-SA (6), C-TAG (4) and Length/Type (2). These map to destinationMacAddress (80), sourceMacAddress (56), dot1qVlanId (243) with dot1qPriority (244), and ethernetType (256).

A service-tagged frame adds a 4-octet S-TAG before the C-TAG, and the C-TAG uses dot1qCustomerVlanId and dot1qCustomerPriority. A backbone-VLAN-tagged frame has B-DA, B-SA, a 4-octet B-TAG, a 16-octet I-TAG, a C-TAG and Length/Type. The I-TAG can be exported whole as dot1qServiceInstanceTag (411) or as a set of 412, 413, 414 and 415.
sections.eli5: This section is a map that matches each part of an Ethernet message to the box on the form where you write it down.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
Reporting more granular data may increase the risk of denial of service attacks against a Collector. Protection is discussed in Section 11.4 of RFC 7011. Apart from that, the document introduces no security issues beyond those in RFC 7011 and RFC 5477.

For IANA, the existing elements were modified as described in Sections 3.1, 4 and 5. Per RFC 7013, RFC 7133 was appended to the Requester, the revision number was incremented by one and the revision date was updated. The new elements were allocated as shown in Section 3.2.
sections.eli5: Counting in more detail makes a bigger pile of paperwork, so the office that reads it could get overwhelmed. Other than that, nothing new is risky.

viz.caption: NEW INFORMATION ELEMENTS FOR SECTIONS AND SERVICE TAGS

items.label: dataLinkFrameType
items.desc: Type of the data link frame; flags 0x01 Ethernet, 0x02 IEEE 802.11.

items.label: sectionOffset
items.desc: Offset into the packet section; defaults to zero.

items.label: sectionExportedOctets
items.desc: Observed length of a packet section when padding is used.

items.label: dot1qServiceInstanceTag
items.desc: The 16-octet I-TAG Tag Control Information field.
